result.title: What's Driving the Gender Gap in the CEO Pipeline?
result.description:
There’s a gender gap in the CEO pipeline.

Chief Operating Officer and Chief Financial Officer are two of the most common routes to becoming a CEO. But women are less represented in these roles, narrowing the pipeline to the top job.

Women hold around a quarter of C-suite roles and a third of board seats, but only 19% of CEO positions and 5% of board chairs.

Find out what it will take to fix the pipeline - not just the headcount - in our report, Closing the Gender Gap in Senior Leadership, which draws on unique data from LinkedIn and Egon Zehnder: https://wef.ch/leadershipgendergap26

result.title: The unstoppable green revolution: Adam Tooze on the "most dramatic story in the history of energy”
result.description:
Conflict in Ukraine and the Middle East have exposed the vulnerability of fossil fuel supply chains and prices. Coupled with Chinese supply of cheap renewables hardware, that makes the transition to green energy unstoppable, despite political resistance in some parts of the world. So says historian and podcaster Adam Tooze, director of the European Institute at Columbia University.
In this wide-ranging interview, recorded at the World Economic Forum's Summer Davos in Dalian, China in June, Tooze also talks about how Europe and China can avoid a massive trade war over cars; the future of economic development in the Global South; and what he sees as the greatest threat to humanity that most of us are choosing to ignore.

result.title: ‘We are going to solve the climate crisis. I have no doubt’
result.description:
Twenty years ago, the film An Inconvenient Truth followed The Climate Reality Project founder and former US vice president Al Gore in his campaign to spread the word about climate change.

That groundbreaking documentary helped usher climate science into the mainstream.

Here, Al Gore shares some reflections on what has changed in the past 20 years - and why he believes that humanity will ultimately triumph over this challenge.

Hear more from Al Gore at the World Economic Forum: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wRKKnaIz2W0

result.title: What 20 years of data on the global gender gap reveals
result.description:
What does 20 years of data on gender equality tell us?

In 2026, nearly 70% of the global gender gap has been closed, the highest level recorded. But progress is far from evenly shared.

And while women now make up almost half of workers entering the labour force, old patterns of gender inequality remain present in the industries of the future.

Two decades after launching the first Global Gender Gap Report, World Economic Forum Managing Director Saadia Zahidi talks us through the findings of the latest report in more detail, and explains how gender parity is a critical foundation of progress worldwide.

Read the Global Gender Gap Report 2026: https://www.weforum.org/publications/global-gender-gap-report-2026

result.title: Japan just hit a new tourism record
result.description:
Japan welcomed a record number of visitors in 2025, after large rises in 2024 and 2023.

Year-on-year growth sounds like a good thing, but there are downsides to new #tourism records.

Some of Japan’s most historic sites, such as Tokyo and Mount Fuji, became overcrowded. So what did Japan do? It took measures to promote its more overlooked regions - including offering free domestic plane tickets.

For more about why #Japan has been crowned the world’s most tourism-ready country, read the World Economic Forum’s Travel and Tourism Development Index 2026: https://www.weforum.org/publications/travel-tourism-development-index-2026/
